---
title: Troubleshooting
description: Find out why a command is greyed, an edit is refused, a file won't open, a clip is silent or an export stops, and what to do next.
---

Frame Job says why it won't do something, in a sentence or a tooltip. This page starts from what you see and tells you what it means and what to do. For the numbers behind these answers, see [Limits](/reference/limits/).

## A command is greyed out

Every menu item has a rule for when it's on. [Menus](/reference/menus/) and [The Clip menu](/reference/clip-menu/) give each item's rule. A ⌘ shortcut does nothing while its item is greyed.

If the item should be on, check these first:

| Check | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| The selection | Many commands need a clip selected, or a certain kind of clip. |
| A sheet | While a sheet is open, every editor command is off. Close the sheet first. |
| A nest | With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, these are off: **New Project from Range…**, **Make Vertical Version…**, **Rename Graphic…**, **Add Marker**, **Next Marker**, **Previous Marker**, **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** and **Text Behind Subject**. Leave the nest with <kbd>⌘↑</kbd>. |
| A text field | **Open Nest**, **Close Nest**, **Delete** and **Ripple Delete** are off while you type, because their keys edit the text. |
| A key | A command that needs your own key stays in the menu, greyed, and its title ends "(needs your AssemblyAI key)". Rest the pointer on it to see which key and where to set it. Saving the key turns it on at once. See [A feature asks for a key](#a-feature-asks-for-a-key). |

## A key does nothing

Single-letter keys and the arrow keys belong to the editor window, and they stand down in two cases.

- **You're typing in a field.** Press <kbd>↩</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>, or click outside the field, to give the keys back to the editor.
- **A sheet is open.** Close it first. In a sheet, <kbd>↩</kbd> presses the default button and <kbd>⎋</kbd> cancels.

Two keys can do something other than what you expect:

- The arrow keys never move a clip on the canvas, even with the canvas focused. They keep moving the playhead. To shift a clip by a set amount, see [Nudge](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/#nudge).
- With a point selected on a [curve](/color/curves/), <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes the point, not the clip.

See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/) and [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/).

## An edit is refused

When the project's rules won't allow an edit, Frame Job beeps, nothing changes, and the rule's own sentence appears at the foot of the inspector after "Refused: ":

> Refused: clips 4 and 7 would overlap by 120000 ticks, more than half of the shorter clip (100000 ticks)

The sentence stays until the project changes or you click it. A [tick](/reference/glossary/#projects-and-the-timeline) is 1/600,000 of a second, so this one says the overlap would be 0.2 s and the shorter clip is 0.17 s long.

The rules you'll meet most:

| Rule | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| The overlap rule | On one track, a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half the length of the shorter clip. |
| A locked track | Its clips can't be dragged, trimmed, slipped or rolled, and you can't insert onto it or close a gap on it. Unlock it with its [lock button](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). |
| The one-frame minimum | Trims and rolls leave a clip at least one frame long. |
| The ends of the file | A media clip can't be trimmed, rolled or slipped past either end of its file. |

Two other results look similar:

- **A beep with no message** means the edit would have changed nothing, such as a slip already at the end of the footage. No rule was broken.
- **An error alert** means Frame Job couldn't use the request at all, such as a pasted value outside its range.

During a drag, positions the rules won't allow are skipped, and the clip waits at the last allowed place. Only the drop counts.

See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).

## A project won't open

A project that can't be read fails with a message naming the problem, and Frame Job doesn't rewrite the package.

| Message | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| "*name* does not contain a readable project.json." | The package has lost its project file, or it's damaged. Open a backup copy if you have one. |
| "project format version *N* is newer than this build understands (version *M*); update Frame Job to open it" | A newer Frame Job saved it. [Update Frame Job](/getting-started/updates/). |
| "too many clips: 5000 (max 4096)", or the same for tracks, markers or media | The file is past one of the [project limits](/reference/limits/#project-size). |

Files that have moved don't stop a project opening, and neither does a damaged `cache/` folder. For moved files, see [Clips show a slate](#clips-show-a-slate). Also see [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/).

## A file won't import

Each refusal names the file and the reason.

| Message | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "*file* is AV1 video, which needs an M3 or later Mac." | This Mac has no AV1 decoder. |
| "*file* is VP9 Profile 1 video, which this Mac cannot decode; VP9 Profiles 0 and 2 import." | Only those two VP9 profiles import. VP8 is refused the same way. |
| "Could not read *file*." | The file is damaged, or it isn't a format Frame Job reads. |
| "*file* has no video or audio the app can open." | The file holds neither. |
| "Timed out reading *file*." | The check took longer than 30 seconds, usually because of a stalled network volume. |
| "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65." | The LUT reader names the line and the problem. See [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/). |
| "Not enough free space to open *file*…" | A WebM or Matroska file needs room for its copy. The sentence says how much. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/). |

A file in a codec this Mac decodes still imports even when some of its data is damaged.

If macOS can't open a file, you can repackage or convert it with your own ffmpeg. See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).

If the **File ▸ Add Media…** panel won't let you choose a file, drop it on the Media tab instead. The panel lists only the common types. See [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/).

An agent's `import_media` reports these reasons too.

## Clips show a slate

A project always opens, even when files it uses have moved or been deleted. Clips whose file is gone keep their place and show a slate, and their rows in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) wear the **missing** badge.

When a project opens with files missing, Frame Job offers the **Missing media** sheet once. Choose **Locate…** for a file. Frame Job also looks in that file's folder for the other missing files by name, so a shoot moved as one folder is usually found in one go. To relink a file later, use **Relink…** on its row in the Media tab. An agent uses `relink_media`.

Two other cases show a slate or leave media missing:

- A reversed clip shows a slate until its backwards copy has been rendered. See [Reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/).
- A movie that was moved out of the Rewrapped folder stays missing until you relink it.

See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).

## A clip is silent

Check these in order. A muted clip, a muted track and a track silenced by a solo all draw the waveform faded.

| Check | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The clip's own sound | The clip may be muted in the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/), or its [sound turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/). |
| The track's **Mute** | A muted track is silent. Mute wins over Solo, so a track that's muted and soloed stays silent. |
| **Solo** on another track | While any track is soloed, the others are silent, even if the soloed track has nothing on it. See [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/). |
| The clip's rate | Above ×12 a clip has no sound, and the Speed section says "Audio is silent above ×12". On a ramped clip, one rate above ×12 anywhere silences the whole clip. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/). |
| Its render | A ramp's sound, and a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off, is silent in the preview until its render finishes. A failed render stays failed until the clip's timing changes or you reopen Frame Job. |
| **Detach Audio** | After a detach, the picture clip's own sound is off, and the sound is on its linked clip. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/). |

If the clip plays but [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) or a [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) has gone, check its speed. Both play only at normal speed, so a clip with a speed change, a ramp or a freeze frame plays without them.

## An export won't start or stops

An export that fails says why and leaves no finished file. An agent reads the same reason from `export_status`.

**Export…** is greyed on an empty project.

"Preparing…" is a wait, not a stall. An export waits for what it has to draw and play first, such as speed-ramp audio, [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) masks, and sound measurements.

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| "Clip *N*'s loudness or speech has not been measured yet…" | An export waits up to five minutes for a measurement still running, then stops. Wait for the clip's Status rows to show its loudness, then export again. |
| "Clip *N*'s retimed audio could not be rendered: …" | A failed render keeps failing exports until you change the clip's timing or reopen Frame Job. |
| "The export was not started: the graphic…" or "The export was stopped at frame *N* of the graphic…" | A graphic that can't draw itself never ships. Fix its [module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) and export again. |
| "This Mac cannot export with the “*preset*” preset." | This Mac has no encoder for that format. Choose [another format](/export/formats/). |
| "An animated GIF is limited to 600 frames and this range is *N*." | Shorten the range, or lower the export frame rate. An APNG has the same limit. See [Animated GIF and PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/). |
| "An export that keeps transparency has to have the canvas's own shape…" | ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha (WebM) won't take a size of a different shape. Use a size from the popup, or one with the same proportions. See [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/). |

A queued AV1 or VP9 job can sit waiting for memory, so it hasn't stalled. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).

:::caution
Quitting during an **Export…** progress sheet doesn't ask first, and it leaves a half-written file. Only the Export Queue is guarded at quit.
:::

See [Export progress and the report](/export/progress-and-report/).

## A feature asks for a key

Anything that sends your words or your audio to a language or cloud model needs your own key. Everything that runs on your Mac needs none.

| Message | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." | Paste a key under **Transcription** in [Settings](/reference/settings/). |
| "No Anthropic API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant." | Paste a key under **Assistant** in Settings. |
| "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" | The key failed. Check it, and press **Verify** to test it. |

A transcript made in one AssemblyAI region can't be seen from the other, so check **Region** too.

An agent can't set a key, so a person has to. See [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/).

## Recording won't start

A recording needs macOS's permissions, and Frame Job asks for each one only when you press Record.

- **Screen Recording** is at **System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording**. Once it's on, relaunch Frame Job if macOS asks, then press Record again. Later presses without it open that pane.
- **Microphone**, **Camera** and **Input Monitoring** are asked for only when the recording needs them.
- If you started Frame Job from a terminal or another app, macOS applies that app's permissions. The panel's note names the launching process and how to relaunch.
- If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, nothing can be recorded until one wakes.

An agent's `record_screen` never asks for a permission, so a person has to grant it first. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).

## An agent can't reach Frame Job

Only programs running as you can connect, through the `framejob-mcp` helper inside the app.

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| The client can't start the helper after you moved Frame Job | Open **Settings**, press **Copy MCP Command** and register the new path. The path is the one you opened Settings from, and it doesn't follow the app. |
| "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job." | The helper isn't in this copy. Use a complete copy of the app. |
| "Frame Job did not answer at…" | Frame Job launched but wasn't listening within 60 seconds. Later calls in that client session don't launch another copy, so quit the stray copy and try again. |

See [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).

## Related

- [Limits](/reference/limits/)
- [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/)
- [Glossary](/reference/glossary/)

---
title: Glossary
description: Frame Job's own words in plain terms, from action and canvas to nest, ramp, stem and tick, each linked to its page.
---

The words Frame Job uses, in plain terms, each with a link to the page that explains it.

## Projects and the timeline

- **Action.** An animation on a clip: a span on its action lane with an end state its properties ease to. See [Actions](/motion/actions/).
- **Adjustment clip.** A clip with no picture of its own that grades every track behind it. See [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/).
- **Canvas.** The fixed frame every clip is composited into. Every export starts from its size. See [The canvas](/canvas/the-canvas/).
- **Clip.** One placed piece on a track: a stretch of a media file, or a text, shape, image, graphic, adjustment or nest clip. See [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/).
- **Current track.** The track of the first selected clip, or with nothing selected the front-most track. Track commands act on it. See [Menus](/reference/menus/).
- **Edit point.** A clip's start or end, where <kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> stop. See [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/).
- **Frame grid.** The frames of the project's rate. Every time you set lands on one. See [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/).
- **Identity.** An edit that was understood and had nothing to change. It makes no undo step and says nothing. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
- **In–Out range.** The span set with <kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd>, which many commands act on. See [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/).
- **Linked pair.** A picture clip and its detached sound, which move, split and ripple together. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
- **Media.** A file the project has imported, listed in the Media tab. Clips refer to it. See [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/).
- **Nest.** A clip that wraps other clips into a timeline of its own. See [Nests](/editing/nests/).
- **Package.** A `.framejob` project, a folder the Finder shows as one file. See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/).
- **Playhead.** The current time on the timeline. See [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/).
- **Refusal.** A rule declining an edit, in that rule's own sentence. Nothing changes and no undo step is made. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
- **Ripple.** An edit that closes the gap it leaves by moving later clips along. See [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/).
- **Selected action.** The one action of the single selected clip that the Clip tab is editing. While it's chosen, the fields show and write its end state. See [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/).
- **Tick.** Frame Job's unit of time, 600,000 to the second, which divides every common frame duration exactly. Refusals and agents speak in ticks. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
- **Track.** A lane of clips. The front track is the top lane, and it's drawn over those behind it. See [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/).

## Picture and sound

- **Camera Log.** A file's setting saying which camera log curve it holds, so it's converted at the start of the picture. See [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/).
- **Cue.** One timed caption. See [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/).
- **Cutout.** A clip with Remove Background on. See [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/).
- **Deep.** More than 8 bits a component. See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/).
- **Ducking.** Lowering a clip's sound under another's. See [Ducking](/audio/ducking/).
- **Dynamic range.** Whether the project works in SDR or HDR (HLG). See [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/).
- **J-cut and L-cut.** The sound of a linked pair starting before, or ending after, its picture. See [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).
- **Look.** A built-in grade or a `.cube` LUT on a clip. See [Looks](/color/looks/).
- **LUFS.** The unit of loudness. See [Normalize](/audio/normalize/).
- **LUT.** A colour lookup table in a `.cube` file. See [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).
- **Matte.** A track that cuts the track behind it by its alpha or brightness. See [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/).
- **Plate.** A clip that fills the canvas behind everything, such as a solid colour or a picture from **Add Background**. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
- **Qualifier.** An adjustment clip's pick of the pixels it grades, by hue, saturation and brightness. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/).
- **Ramp.** A speed change over time, a Speed action on the action lane. See [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/).
- **Scopes.** The waveform, parade, vectorscope and histogram beside the preview. See [Scopes](/color/scopes/).
- **Slate.** What a clip draws in place of a picture it doesn't have, such as missing media. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
- **Stem.** One track's sound written as its own file beside the mix. See [Audio stems](/export/stems/).
- **Transition.** The change from one clip to the next across their overlap on one track. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).

## Graphics and agents

- **Assistant.** The chat in the inspector that edits the open project on your own Anthropic key. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/).
- **Category.** The list a module is filed under in the Graphic dialog. See [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/).
- **Error card.** What a graphic draws in its own box when it can't draw itself. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
- **Graphic.** A clip whose picture is drawn by code. It's the clip's content, not an effect. See [What a graphic is](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/).
- **Graphic package.** A `.fjgraphic` file holding a module and the fonts and pictures it uses. See [Share a graphic](/graphics/share-a-graphic/).
- **Kept revision.** An earlier text of a module the app kept, the last 10 for each module. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
- **MCP.** The protocol an agent uses to drive Frame Job, through the `framejob-mcp` helper. See [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/).
- **Module.** A graphic's source, one JavaScript module returning SVG for each frame. See [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/).
- **Op.** One edit to a project, applied whole. An agent's tools mostly each send one. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).
- **Patch.** A partial object a caller writes to say what to change. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/).
- **Props.** The values a graphic is drawn with, stored on its clip. See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/).
- **Template.** A module the app ships, copied into the package when you insert it. See [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/).

title: Open source and notices
description: Frame Job's Apache License 2.0, and where to read the third-party notices every copy of the app carries.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Frame Job is open source. This page gives its licence, and says where to find the notices for the third-party software it includes.

<AtAGlance
  where="Frame Job.app ▸ Contents/Resources/Acknowledgements.txt"
/>

## Frame Job's licence

Frame Job is released under the Apache License, Version 2.0. The full text is the [LICENSE file](https://github.com/kpgalligan/framejob/blob/main/LICENSE) at the root of the repository.

## Third-party notices

Every copy of the app carries `Acknowledgements.txt`, which lists every third-party notice the app owes, each with its licence text. It's written at each build, from the Rust crates, the Assistant helper's npm packages, Bun, Sparkle, the encoders, the voice-activity model and the fonts.

There's no entry for it in the About panel. To read it:

<Steps>

1. In the Finder, right-click Frame Job and choose **Show Package Contents**.

2. Open `Contents/Resources/Acknowledgements.txt`.

</Steps>

## What carries its own licence

Some of what ships with Frame Job keeps its own licence, beside it in the app or listed in `Acknowledgements.txt`.

| Part | Licence | Where its text is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fonts: Anton, Bebas Neue, Darker Grotesque, IBM Plex Mono, Montserrat, Source Sans 3 and Source Serif 4 | SIL Open Font License | `Contents/Resources/Fonts/`, one `OFL-` file for each family |
| The voice-activity model, Silero VAD | MIT | `Contents/Resources/Models/LICENSE` |
| SVT-AV1 and libvpx, the [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/) encoders | BSD 3-Clause Clear and BSD 3-Clause | `Contents/Resources/Licenses/svt-av1/` and `Contents/Resources/Licenses/libvpx/`, with their patent texts |
| A patched copy of tiny-skia, which draws [graphics](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/) | BSD 3-Clause | `Acknowledgements.txt` |

The published app also includes Sparkle, for [updates](/getting-started/updates/). A copy you build yourself has no updater.

## Related

- [Requirements and install](/getting-started/requirements-and-install/)
- [Updates](/getting-started/updates/)

title: Limits
description: Every hard number in Frame Job in one place, from how many clips a project holds to each area's ceilings.
---

The hard numbers, in one place. Each section gives an area's ceilings and links to the page that explains them. For what to do when you hit one, see [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/).

## Project size

| A project holds at most | |
| --- | --- |
| Clips | 4,096 |
| Tracks | 64 |
| Markers | 1,024 |
| Media files | 1,024 |
| Levels of nesting | 8 |

Clips and tracks inside [nests](/editing/nests/) count towards the same totals.

An edit that would go past one of these isn't made, and an alert names the limit, for example "too many clips: 4097 (max 4096)". A project file already past a limit won't open, the message names the limit, and the package isn't rewritten.

A [recording](/recording/where-it-lands/) that needs a new track can't be added to a project at its track limit. Its files stay on disk and the note names them.

Files in a project have one more limit: a [`.cube` LUT](#colour) can be at most 32 MiB.

## Canvas and layers

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| [Canvas](/projects/canvas-size/) width and height | Even numbers, 16 to 16,384 px |
| [Scale](/canvas/transform/) | 1 to 1,000 % |
| [Shape](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) width and height | 1 to 20,000 px in the fields. A drag on the canvas stops at 4 and 20,000 px. |
| [Filters](/effects/filters/) on one clip | 4 |
| [Obscure](/effects/obscure/) regions on one clip | 4 |
| An obscure region's width and height | 1 to 20,000 source pixels |
| [Gradient](/text-and-shapes/gradients/) stops | 2 to 8 |
| [Preview zoom](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/) steps | Fit, 50%, 100%, 200% |

Scale is uniform for pictures. Only a shape's box and a text clip's wrap width can be stretched on one axis.

Crop, Corner Radius and Chroma Key work only on video, image and still clips. A nest clip can't take a [blend mode](/canvas/blend-modes/), and Add Blurred Background isn't offered for one.

## Timeline and editing

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Overlaps | On one track, a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half the length of the shorter clip |
| Shortest clip after a trim or roll | 1 frame |
| [Timeline zoom](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) | 0.35 to 4,000 points per second, 42 by default |
| [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/) radius | 8 points, on the timeline and on the [canvas](/canvas/canvas-snapping/) |

A media clip can't be trimmed, rolled or slipped past either end of its file. Every time you set lands on the project's frame grid. See [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/).

[Markers](/timeline/markers/) live on the main timeline only. Inside a nest you can't add one, step to one or jump to one, though the Document tab can still rename, chapter and delete them. Only an agent can change a marker's colour.

## Speed

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Slowest rate | ×0.1 |
| Fastest rate | ×1000 |
| Fastest rate with sound | ×12, with Keep pitch on or off |
| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) length, when none is given | 2 s |
| [Speed Ramp…](/speed/make-a-ramp/) **Hold** | None, 25%, 50% or 75%, 50% by default. An agent can use any hold from 0 to 0.9. |

Frame Job asks before an edit takes a clip with sound past ×12. On a ramped clip, one rate above ×12 anywhere silences the whole clip. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).

With Keep pitch on, a ramp's sound can lag the picture by up to about 22 ms after a steep slow-down. See [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/).

## Audio

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| [Clip volume](/audio/volume/) | Up to 3200 % (about +30 dB). The slider covers 0 to 400 %, and the field takes the rest. |
| [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/) | +30.1 dB to −60 dB |
| [Track volume](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/) | Up to +12 dB (×4) |
| [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) drift correction | Up to 0.2 % from ×1 |
| [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) | Matches with the [EQ](/audio/eq/)'s five shelves and bands |

The [gate](/audio/gate/), the [leveller](/audio/leveller/) and the [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) need a measured clip. A clip shorter than 0.4 s, or too quiet to measure, plays and exports without them. An export waits up to five minutes for a measurement still running, then stops and names the clip.

A file with more than two channels is measured from a two-channel mix of it. The [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) reads only the first two channels of a track with more.

See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).

## Captions

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Longest file [AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) takes | 10 hours |
| **Vocabulary** terms | 1,000 |
| [Caption import](/captions/import-captions/) | SubRip only |

AssemblyAI uploads and bills each whole media file. Two media entries over the same file are uploaded and billed separately.

Captions are burned-in text clips, never a switchable subtitle stream.

A clip played in reverse, a clip with its audio off, and a clip whose media is missing or silent can't be transcribed. See [What can be transcribed](/captions/what-can-be-transcribed/).

## Colour

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Points on a [curve](/color/curves/) | 2 to 16 |
| [`.cube` LUT](/color/luts/) | 3D only, size 2 to 65, file up to 32 MiB |
| [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) override | 1 to 10,000 cd/m² |
| SDR reference white in an HDR project | Fixed at 203 cd/m² |

An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) can't go inside a nest, take a transition or overlap another clip on its track. Blur, sharpen, pixelate and blend modes aren't available on it.

The Color tab needs every selected clip to be gradable, so deselect text, shape, graphic and nest clips first.

[Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/) exist only on adjustment clips. There is no Offset wheel.

## Export

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| [Custom size](/export/size/) | 16 to 8,192 px on each edge |
| [Animated GIF or PNG](/export/gif-and-apng/) | 600 frames: 48 s at GIF's 12.5 fps, or 24 s at APNG's 25 fps |
| [Loudness target](/export/loudness/) | At most 40 dB of gain. A target further above the mix lands quieter than asked. |
| Master limiter | Can't be turned off. 0 dBTP is its loosest ceiling. |
| 24-bit sound | WAV and AIFF only. The sound is never dithered. |
| [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/) file size | The rate is a soft cap. Very detailed footage can come in up to about 1.25 times over it with AV1, and 1.15 times with VP9. |

[ProRes 4444, HEVC with Alpha and VP9 with Alpha (WebM)](/export/transparency/) won't export at a custom size of a different shape from the canvas. VP9 with Alpha (WebM) is 8-bit SDR only.

On an M1 or M2 Mac, Frame Job can't play or re-import its own AV1 file.

Queued jobs run one at a time. A queued AV1 or VP9 job waits while those already running would use more than a quarter of the Mac's memory with it. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).

## Graphics

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Largest [graphic](/graphics/size-and-timing/) | 8,192 px on a side |
| [Property](/graphics/properties/) values on one clip | 64 |
| Options on one property | 32 |
| Characters in a string property | 4,096 |
| [Kept versions](/graphics/manage-graphics/) of each module | The last 10 |
| Files watched one by one | The first 16 module, font and picture files |
| [Memory for drawn frames](/graphics/playback-and-memory/) | A quarter of the Mac's memory |

In a folder with more than 16 files, a save that rewrites a later file in place may not show until something else in the folder changes.

## Recording

- A [camera](/recording/record-a-camera/) records at one of its formats, at that format's highest frame rate.
- The panel offers five [camera layouts](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/), and a corner layout is always the bottom-right one.
- There's no global shortcut to stop. Use the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) or the **File** menu.
- A recording longer than 9:59:59 shows a label wider than the menu-bar item was sized for.
- If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, nothing can be recorded until one wakes. See [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/).

## Assistant and agents

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| [Compaction](/assistant/context-and-compaction/) threshold | 20,000 to 900,000 tokens, 300,000 by default |
| **Clear old tool results** | Past 150,000 tokens, when it's ticked |
| Wait for a launched copy to start listening | 60 seconds |
| Wait for `get_media_analysis` | 60 seconds |

If Frame Job launches but isn't listening within 60 seconds, the call says so, and later calls in that client session don't launch another copy.

Agent calls run one at a time, and any call waits while you hold the mouse down mid-drag. See [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/).

`get_media_analysis` keeps what it covered in its 60 seconds, then stops and says how much that was. See [What the Assistant can do](/assistant/what-it-can-do/) for the Assistant's own limits.

## Settings

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| [Background render](/reference/settings/)'s **Start after** | 1 to 60 seconds, 5 by default |
| Inspector width | 280 to 440 points |
| Timeline height | 140 points to 60 % of the window |

[Converting on import](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) needs `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe`. Frame Job looks on your `PATH`, then in `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/local/bin`, `/usr/bin` and `/bin`. For an install anywhere else, run this in Terminal:

```sh
defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegPath /path/to/ffmpeg
```

`ffprobe` is taken from beside it, or else found by the same search.

## Related

- [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/)
- [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/)
- [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/)

    /// The refusal sentence for a video track that will not decode.
    static func refusal(
        fileName: String, codec: FourCharCode, vp9Profile: Int?, av1Hardware: Bool
    ) -> String {
        switch codec {
        case kCMVideoCodecType_AV1 where !av1Hardware:
            return "\(fileName) is AV1 video, which needs an M3 or later Mac."
        case kCMVideoCodecType_AV1:
            return "\(fileName) is AV1 video, which this Mac cannot decode."
        case kCMVideoCodecType_VP9:
            if let profile = vp9Profile, profile == 1 || profile == 3 {
                return "\(fileName) is VP9 Profile \(profile) video, which this Mac cannot decode;"
                    + " VP9 Profiles 0 and 2 import."
            }
            return "\(fileName) is VP9 video, which this Mac cannot decode."
        case vp8:
            return "\(fileName) is VP8 video, which this Mac cannot decode."
        case 0:
            return "\(fileName) is video this Mac cannot decode."
        default:
            let code = String([24, 16, 8, 0].map {
                Character(Unicode.Scalar(UInt8((codec >> UInt32($0)) & 0xFF)))
            })
            return "\(fileName) is '\(code)' video, which this Mac cannot decode."
        }
    }

2:title: Keys and typing
8:Frame Job plays on <kbd>Space</kbd> and trims on <kbd>W</kbd>, so a letter means one thing on the timeline and another in a text field. The rule is short: the keys belong to the editor unless you're typing or a sheet is open.
11:  keys={['Space', '↩', 'Tab', '⎋']}
41:They never fire while you're typing. While a sheet is open none of them works, in either window, so the project can't change underneath the sheet. In the Preview Window they also do nothing while a field in the editor window is still being typed in.
62:## Start and finish typing
64:A field takes the keys only when you click in it, or choose a command that opens one for typing, such as **Clip ▸ Rename…** or **View ▸ Assistant**. Nothing else moves the keyboard into a field, so you won't type into one by accident.
71:| Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> or <kbd>⇧Tab</kbd> | Any text, including the Assistant's message field |
74:<kbd>Tab</kbd> doesn't step through fields. With macOS Full Keyboard Access on, it does, and walks to the next control instead.
76:A click on the title bar doesn't end your typing. Neither does a click on the field's own margins or on a text view's scroller, because they count as part of the field. A click on a field's [quick-pick chevron](/getting-started/inspector-fields/#use-a-quick-pick) applies what you typed, then opens its menu.
78:While an input method is composing, <kbd>↩</kbd> and <kbd>Tab</kbd> belong to it.
82:These four keys act on the timeline when you're not typing. In a text field their menu items switch off, so the keys keep their usual text meaning and a slip of the finger can't delete a clip.

def cargo_packages(metadata: dict) -> list:
    """Package dicts reachable from resolve.root over non-dev edges, FIRST_PARTY removed."""
    packages = {p["id"]: p for p in metadata["packages"]}
    nodes = {n["id"]: n for n in metadata["resolve"]["nodes"]}
    seen, stack = set(), [metadata["resolve"]["root"]]
    while stack:
        current = stack.pop()
        if current not in seen:
            seen.add(current)
            stack += [d["pkg"] for d in nodes[current].get("deps", []) if MUTANT == "dev-edges"
                      or any(k.get("kind") != "dev" for k in d.get("dep_kinds", []))]
    return [packages[i] for i in sorted(seen) if packages[i]["name"] not in FIRST_PARTY]


def npm_packages(lock_text: str) -> list:
    """[(name, version, folder)] from workspaces[""].dependencies through each package's
    "dependencies"; not devDependencies, not optionalPeers. A dependency resolves as Node does:
    bun's nested key under the dependent's own chain (`a/b/c`), else under each shorter chain
    (`a/c`), else the hoisted `c`; `folder` is its folder under agent/
    (`node_modules/a/node_modules/c`)."""
    lock = json.loads(re.sub(r",(\s*[}\]])", r"\1", lock_text))
    entries, found = lock.get("packages", {}), {}
    stack = [((), name) for name in sorted(lock["workspaces"][""].get("dependencies", {}))]
    while stack:
        chain, name = stack.pop()
        paths = [chain[:level] + (name,) for level in range(len(chain), -1, -1)]
        path = next((p for p in paths if "/".join(p) in entries), None)
        if path is None:
            raise Failed(f"acknowledgements: {name} is not in agent/bun.lock's packages")
        key = "/".join(path)
        if key in found:
            continue
        entry = entries[key]
        folder = "/".join(f"node_modules/{part}" for part in path)
        found[key] = (name, entry[0].rsplit("@", 1)[1], folder)
        meta = entry[2] if len(entry) > 2 and isinstance(entry[2], dict) else {}
        stack += [(path, dep) for dep in sorted(meta.get("dependencies", {}))]
    return sorted(set(found.values()))

The message stays until the project changes (an edit, an undo or redo, or going into or out of a nest) or until you click it. Moving the playhead or changing the selection doesn't clear it.

Three things take <kbd>Space</kbd> or the arrows for themselves:

- In a text field, <kbd>Space</kbd> types a space.
- With macOS Full Keyboard Access on, a focused button, pop-up or segmented control keeps <kbd>Space</kbd> to press itself.
- With the preview canvas focused, a tap of <kbd>Space</kbd> plays or pauses when you release it, because holding it down arms [panning](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/). A <kbd>Space</kbd> held to pan doesn't change playback.

docs/guide/editing.md:279 says 'a pasted value outside its allowed range' shows an error alert. Inspector fields clamp what they commit (app/Sources/OptionControls.swift:232-237), so the pasted-value example isn't supported.
